intent_record.intent_summary: Prevents race conditions during PTP disable by synchronizing pending IRQs.
intent_record.what: In the else branch of ptp_ocp_ts_enable, added retrieval of the PCI IRQ vector, a read-back of reg->intr_mask, and a conditional synchronize_irq call.
intent_record.how: Guarantees completion of any active interrupt handlers before disabling further operations, avoiding concurrent access issues.

intent_record.intent_summary: Corrects driver detachment by ensuring timestampers are disabled, the PTP clock is unregistered, and memory is freed.
intent_record.what: Added conditional logic in ptp_ocp_detach to disable interrupts on timestampers (ts0-ts4, pps), unregister the PTP clock, and free pin configuration memory.
intent_record.how: Ensures hardware interrupts are stopped and kernel resources are released during driver removal, preventing race conditions, resource leaks, or use-after-free errors.

vuln_statements.explanation: In the driver cleanup/removal path, deleting the watchdog timer synchronously can create a race condition or use-after-free vulnerability. If the timer callback is executing when timer_delete_sync() is called, or if other code paths still reference the bp structure after this point, accessing freed memory can occur. The timing of timer deletion relative to other resource deallocations (sysfs detachment, attribute group deletion) is critical - improper ordering here allows concurrent access to partially freed structures.
